sets.title: Market structure essentials
sets.subject: Economics
sets.description: Original introductory practice: competition, entry barriers and price discrimination.

items.prompt: What is a price taker?
items.answer: A seller that accepts the market price because it cannot individually influence that price.

items.prompt: What is a barrier to entry?
items.answer: An obstacle that makes it difficult for new firms to enter a market.

items.prompt: What is product differentiation?
items.answer: Differences, real or perceived, between the products offered by different sellers.

items.prompt: What is price discrimination?
items.answer: Selling the same product at different prices when the price differences are not explained by cost differences.

items.prompt: Which feature best fits perfect competition?
items.explanation: Perfect competition is characterised by many sellers offering a homogeneous product.

items.prompt: Which is an example of a legal barrier to entry?
items.explanation: A patent grants legal protection that can prevent competitors from using the protected invention.

items.prompt: Why does preventing resale help price discrimination?
choices: It stops lower-price customers reselling to higher-price customers
items.explanation: Resale would undermine separate prices by allowing higher-price customers to buy through the lower-price group.

sets.title: Algebra without the usual traps
sets.subject: Mathematics
sets.description: Expansion, factorisation and checking quadratic roots. Try each calculation before flipping.

items.prompt: Simplify (1 + x)^2 - (1 - x)^2.
items.answer: 4x. Expand both brackets, then distribute the minus sign to every term in the second bracket.

items.prompt: Factorise a^2 - b^2.
items.answer: (a + b)(a - b)

items.prompt: What does b^2 - 4ac tell you about a quadratic equation?
items.answer: Positive: two distinct real roots. Zero: one repeated real root. Negative: no real roots.

items.prompt: Factorise (x + y)^2 + c(x + y).
items.answer: (x + y)(x + y + c). Treat x + y as one common factor.

items.prompt: Expand (x - 3)^2.
items.explanation: Use (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2. The middle term is -6x.

items.prompt: How many real roots does x^2 + x + 6 = 0 have?
items.explanation: The discriminant is 1 - 24 = -23, which is negative.

sets.title: Conditionals: from facts to regrets
sets.subject: English
sets.description: Practise common conditional patterns and choose the form that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: What is the usual zero conditional pattern?
items.answer: If + present simple, present simple. Example: If water reaches its boiling point, it boils.

items.prompt: What is a common first conditional pattern?
items.answer: If + present simple, will + base verb. Example: If I finish early, I will call you.

items.prompt: How do we describe an unreal present situation?
items.answer: If + past simple, would + base verb. Example: If I had more time, I would practise daily.

items.prompt: How do we describe an unreal past situation?
items.answer: If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Example: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the bus.

items.prompt: If she had studied, she ___ the test.
items.explanation: Both the condition and its imagined result refer to the past, so use the third conditional.

items.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
items.explanation: This is a possible future condition: present simple in the if-clause, will in the main clause.

sets.title: Natural spoken English
sets.subject: English
sets.description: Revise natural conversational expressions from the Obsidian note “Vocab list（口語）”.

items.prompt: How can you naturally say “I decided to give it a try”?
items.answer: I’d shoot my shot. Use it when taking a chance, especially when success is uncertain.

items.prompt: How can you say “I was really surprised” more vividly?
items.answer: I was blown away. It expresses strong surprise or admiration.

items.prompt: How can you say “I started feeling nervous about how others saw me”?
items.answer: I started getting really self-conscious.

items.prompt: What expression means “I could hardly believe it was real”?
items.answer: I remember really pinching myself. It describes a moment that felt almost unreal.

items.prompt: How can you say “I said yes immediately”?
items.answer: I said yes on the spot. “On the spot” means right then and there.

sets.title: Paper 3B: useful phrases
sets.subject: English
sets.description: Practise expressions for promotional articles and proposals from the Obsidian note “Fancy phrases(paper 3b)”.

items.prompt: Write a question opening for a promotional article that highlights two benefits.
items.answer: Fancy a chance to [benefit] while [another benefit]?

items.prompt: Introduce an event and explain the purpose of its activities.
items.answer: This year, [organisation] is bringing back [event], with an exciting range of activities designed to [purpose].

items.prompt: Show that an event offers more than one opportunity.
items.answer: This is more than just a chance to [first benefit]; it is also an opportunity to [second benefit].

items.prompt: Close a promotional article with an invitation to attend.
items.answer: With so much on offer, [event] is certainly not to be missed. So, what are you waiting for? Join us and experience it for yourself!

items.prompt: State the purpose and scope of a proposal.
items.answer: This proposal aims to outline the proposed arrangement, explain its key benefits and provide reasons for its implementation.

items.prompt: Recommend an action in view of a problem or finding.
items.answer: In view of [problem/finding], [action] would be a suitable way to [purpose].

items.prompt: Introduce two reasons supporting a proposal.
items.answer: The rationale behind this proposal is twofold.

items.prompt: Justify the most practical option given a constraint.
items.answer: Considering [constraint], [option] appears to be the most practical choice.
